# Government Benefits Portal — Pre-VPAT Accessibility Audit Plan > **Canonical path:** `docs/a11y-plans/2026-07-28-benefits-portal-pre-vpat-audit-a11y-plan.md` > **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol, AUDIT-SCOPE MODE (WCAG-EM). Review with a11y-critic at the four checkpoints below. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 Level AA (55 success criteria) — see §1.2 for an unresolved conflict with the specified VPAT edition > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users (desktop + mobile), keyboard-only users, low-vision / magnification users, users with limited manipulation, voice-input users, Deaf and hard-of-hearing users, users with cognitive/language/learning disabilities > **Assistive technologies:** NVDA + Chrome, JAWS + Chrome, VoiceOver + Safari (macOS), VoiceOver + Safari (iOS), TalkBack + Chrome (Android), keyboard-only, Dragon NaturallySpeaking, Windows High Contrast / forced-colors, browser zoom to 400% **Feature:** A systematic WCAG 2.2 AA conformance evaluation of a 20-view government benefits portal, executed by two QA engineers over 13 weeks, producing a defensible VPAT. **Risk Level:** HIGH — multi-page authenticated transactional flows, legal disclosure output, external deadline, thin team. **Component Type:** Audit / conformance evaluation (not a component build). Nine planning phases apply, reframed as *evaluation design* rather than *implementation design*; AUDIT-SCOPE MODE layers WCAG-EM on top. --- ## How to read this plan The nine planner phases normally answer "how do we build this correctly?" For an audit they answer a different question: **"what is the correct behavior we are measuring against, on which samples, by which method, and what is the pass/fail rule?"** Each of Phases 2–7 below therefore produces a *reference model* (what conformant looks like for this portal's patterns) plus an *evaluation procedure* (how a QA engineer with basic accessibility knowledge confirms or refutes it). Phase 8 carries the sampling and tooling. Phase 9 carries the work packages. Three failure modes this plan is explicitly designed against, because they are what makes audit output dead: 1. **Findings that restate rule IDs.** "Fails 4.1.2 on 14 pages" is a count, not a finding. Every finding must name the person who is blocked and what they experience. 2. **VPAT boilerplate.** Functional Performance Criteria entries that read "Supports" with no evidence are the single most common defect in real VPATs. §VPAT below makes FPC entries evidence-gated. 3. **Per-page duplication.** The mega-menu is one defect, not twenty. Counting it twenty times inflates the report and buries the eleven distinct problems underneath it. --- ## Scope & Context ### 1.1 What is being evaluated, and for whom **What:** A live, four-year-old, server-rendered government benefits portal with progressive JavaScript enhancement — 20 views, 8 shared component patterns, 3 third-party integrations — evaluated for WCAG 2.2 AA conformance ahead of a VPAT publication in three months. **User need:** Citizens applying for public assistance. This is a consequential-transaction product: failure to complete the application is not an inconvenience, it is a denial of access to benefits. That fact drives the entire prioritization model in this plan (§Severity). It also means the *authenticated application process*, not the home page, is the center of gravity. **Who needs accessibility here — with portal-specific reasons, not a generic list:** | User group | Why this portal specifically | |---|---| | Screen reader users, desktop | 6-step form, data tables, validation errors, session timeout — the highest-density SR risk on the site | | Screen reader users, mobile | Benefits applicants skew mobile-only; iOS VO and TalkBack are primary, not secondary | | Keyboard-only | Mega-menu, date picker, file upload, modal — four custom widgets, four chances for a keyboard trap | | Low vision / magnification | Reflow at 400% on a 6-step form with a sticky header (2.4.11 risk); contrast on status badges | | Limited manipulation | 2.5.8 target size on the date picker grid; 2.5.7 dragging on a drag-and-drop uploader | | Voice input (Dragon) | 2.5.3 Label in Name across every icon-only control; a voice user who says "click Submit" needs the visible word "Submit" in the accessible name | | Deaf / hard of hearing | Embedded program videos — captions are a *first-party* obligation (see §Third-Party) | | Cognitive / language / learning | Error recovery, timeouts, plain language. Also Revised Section 508 FPC 302.9, which no single WCAG AA criterion covers | ### 1.2 Conformance target — and one conflict that must be resolved in Week 1 **Stated target:** WCAG 2.2 Level AA. **Stated template:** VPAT 2.4 Rev 508. These are not aligned, and shipping them together would produce a misleading disclosure. - Revised Section 508 incorporates **WCAG 2.0** Level A and AA by reference. A **Rev 508** edition VPAT is therefore anchored on WCAG 2.0's 38 A/AA criteria, plus Revised 508 Chapters 3–6. - WCAG 2.2 Level A + AA contains **55** criteria: the 38 from 2.0, **minus 4.1.1 Parsing** (obsoleted in WCAG 2.2), **plus 18** criteria introduced in WCAG 2.1 and 2.2. (38 − 1 + 18 = 55.) - Those 18 include the ones most likely to bite this portal: 1.4.10 Reflow, 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus, 2.5.3 Label in Name, 4.1.3 Status Messages, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), 3.2.6 Consistent Help, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum). **A Rev 508 VPAT has no tables for those 18.** Evaluating against WCAG 2.2 and then reporting on a WCAG 2.0-anchored template silently discards the majority of what this audit will find. **Recommended resolution (decide with the commissioner in Week 1, record the decision in the report):** - **Option A (recommended).** Produce the VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 as required for the Section 508 obligation, **plus a clearly labeled supplementary WCAG 2.2 AA conformance table** covering the 18 additional criteria, using the identical Supports / Partially Supports / Does Not Support / Not Applicable / Not Evaluated vocabulary. Report 4.1.1 Parsing in the Rev 508 table (still required by the 2.0 anchor) with a note that it is obsoleted in WCAG 2.2. - **Option B.** Move to a VPAT edition whose WCAG tables reach 2.2 (an INT or WCAG edition at 2.5), and keep the 508 chapters. Cleaner document, but changes a procurement artifact the agency may have already committed to. - **Do not** silently downgrade the evaluation to WCAG 2.0 to fit the template. That is the failure mode this section exists to prevent. *Documentation note:* the template is published by **ITI** (Information Technology Industry Council). Cite it correctly in the report — "ITTF" will read as an error to a federal reviewer. *Confidence:* High on the WCAG criterion arithmetic and on Rev 508's WCAG 2.0 anchor. Moderate on which specific 2.x edition/revision the agency's procurement office will accept — that is a commissioner decision, not a technical one. **Methodology reference:** WCAG-EM. Run **WCAG-EM 2.0** ("WCAG Evaluation Methodology", W3C Group Note, 2026 — https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-em-2/) as the operative methodology, because EM 1.0 predates WCAG 2.1/2.2. Cross-reference **EM 1.0** step numbers (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG-EM/) in the report so a reviewer who expects the 2014 methodology can follow the sample rationale. Neither is normative — conformance is defined by WCAG itself; EM supplies the sampling and reporting discipline. Say this explicitly in the report so no one reads "WCAG-EM conformant" as a conformance claim. ### 1.3 Accessibility support baseline (EM Step 1) — agree and freeze in Week 1 The baseline is a *contract*, not a preference. Every outcome in the VPAT is only claimed for these combinations. | Platform | Browser | AT | Role | |---|---|---|---| | Windows 11 | Chrome (current stable) | NVDA (current stable) | **Primary** — used on every sample | | Windows 11 | Chrome (current stable) | JAWS (current stable) | Secondary desktop — Tier 1 + shared components | | macOS (current) | Safari | VoiceOver | Second engine (WebKit) — Tier 1 + shared components + 3 public views | | iOS (current) | Safari | VoiceOver | Mobile — mobile-critical journey | | Android (current) | Chrome | TalkBack | Mobile — mobile-critical journey | | Windows 11 | Chrome | Dragon NaturallySpeaking | Voice — 2.5.3 spot-checks on all interactive-dense views | | Windows 11 | Chrome / Edge | Forced-colors (High Contrast) | No AT — visual-mode check | | Any | Chrome | None (keyboard only) | Every sample | Record **exact version numbers** at the start and again at the end of the evaluation. If versions change mid-audit, note it; a JAWS update can change announcement behavior and invalidate a finding. If a tool is added mid-evaluation, the baseline is extended and previously evaluated samples are re-checked against the addition, or the addition is declared as covering only samples from that date forward. Do not quietly widen the baseline. **Mobile SR testing must be on physical devices.** TalkBack behavior in emulators is not representative. Budget two devices (one iOS, one Android) in Week 1 procurement — this is a schedule risk if agency device provisioning is slow. ### 1.4 Additional requirements (EM Step 1) - **Report template:** ITI VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 (+ supplementary WCAG 2.2 AA table per §1.2). - **Issue granularity:** one finding per **defect in a source location**, not per instance. A shared-component defect is one finding with an instance list. A content defect (a specific image missing alt text) is one finding per instance, grouped by content type. Every finding carries a stable identifier so the same defect keeps the same ID across the audit and any re-test. - **Required evidence per finding:** view URL (or process step + preceding actions), element selector/XPath, rendered HTML snippet, WCAG SC, tool rule ID where automated, severity, frequency/reach, and — for SR findings — the AT + browser + version and a verbatim announcement transcript. - **Deliverables:** (1) VPAT + supplementary table; (2) findings register; (3) sample set documentation with selection method; (4) evaluation methods statement; (5) prioritized remediation backlog; (6) optional public accessibility statement draft. ### 1.5 Explore (EM Step 2) — the five lists that drive sampling **(a) Common views:** global shell (header, mega-menu, search, footer), content page template, program-detail template, listing template, form-step template, dashboard template, authenticated shell. **(b) Essential functionality:** create an account; sign in; complete and submit a 6-step benefits application; upload supporting documents; check application status; read and act on notifications; find program eligibility information; contact the agency. **(c) Variety of view types:** static content (Home, About), long-form informational (Program Detail ×3 variants), list/index (Program Listings, News), Q&A/accordion (FAQ), forms (Contact, Account creation, Login, 6 application steps), file handling (Document upload), data table (Application status / history), notification list (Notification center). **(d) Technologies relied upon:** HTML, CSS, JavaScript (progressive enhancement), WAI-ARIA, and — declare explicitly — whether conformance *relies on* JavaScript. Server-rendered + progressive enhancement suggests a no-JS baseline may exist. **Test with JavaScript disabled on one Tier-1 process.** If the application form is unusable without JS, that is fine for conformance (JS is an accessibility-supported technology) but it must be declared, not assumed. **(e) Other relevant views:** login/authentication (already listed), the Contact page as the help mechanism for **3.2.6 Consistent Help**, and — **missing from the brief** — an accessibility statement page. If none exists, that is not a WCAG AA failure but it is a gap a federal reviewer will notice; recommend drafting one as an audit deliverable. ### 1.6 Scope gaps to resolve before Week 1 work begins The brief is under-specified in five ways that each change the sample set. Resolve all five with the commissioner; do not start evaluating around them. 1. **Electronic documents.** Benefits portals almost always serve PDFs — application forms, notice letters, eligibility guides, program fact sheets. The brief lists none. Section 508 covers electronic content including documents. A VPAT that silently omits downloadable PDFs is incomplete, and PDF remediation cannot be absorbed late in a 13-week schedule. **Ask directly: does the portal serve PDFs or Office documents? How many, and are they in scope?** If yes and they are in scope, either extend the timeline or scope them out *explicitly and in writing*, and say so in the VPAT's scope declaration. 2. **Language versions.** Government benefits portals commonly publish Spanish (or other language) content. The brief does not say. If a translated version exists, either it is in scope (roughly doubling content-view sampling and requiring 3.1.1/3.1.2 checks on both) or it is excluded in the scope declaration. Excluding *parts* of a product conflicts with WCAG's full-page and complete-process conformance requirements, so an exclusion must be a whole, separately addressable product boundary — e.g. "the Spanish-language site at /es is not covered by this report." 3. **Native mobile app.** iOS VoiceOver and TalkBack are in the AT list. Confirm this means responsive web on mobile, not a native app. If a native app exists, the Playwright/axe/CDP measurement stack cannot touch it, and Chapters 4/5 of the 508 report change materially. 4. **Authenticated data states.** The audit needs test accounts that can reach: new/empty, in-progress application (each of the 6 steps), submitted, additional-documents-requested, approved, denied, and expired-session. Provisioning these is a Week-1 blocker owned by the portal team, not by QA. Empty states and error states are where 4.1.3, 3.3.1 and 3.3.3 failures live; without seeded accounts those criteria come back `cantTell`. 5. **Does the site have a dark mode?** The brief does not say. Do not audit for a mode that does not exist. Forced-colors / Windows High Contrast Mode **is** in scope regardless, because government users use it heavily. ### 1.7 Risk level and a feasibility check the schedule needs before Week 1 **Risk: HIGH.** Multi-page authenticated transactional flows, complete-process conformance, a legally consequential output document, a fixed external deadline, and a two-person team. The brief asks for a plan a two-engineer team can execute in three months. Here is the arithmetic, so the constraint is argued rather than assumed. - 13 weeks × 2 engineers ≈ **26 engineer-weeks**. At ~30 productive hours/week ≈ **780 hours**. - Non-evaluation load: setup, baseline freeze, tool configuration, test-account provisioning, calibration (~60h); VPAT drafting, review, and revision (~80h); findings triage and register maintenance (~60h). **Leaves ≈ 580 hours of evaluation.** - Evaluation load (single primary-SR pass): Tier 1 — 11 views (account creation, login, 6 form steps, document upload, plus the process-level sequence work) at ~8h = **88h**; 8 shared components at ~8h deep-evaluation each = **64h**; Tier 3 — 2 authenticated views at ~6h = **12h**; Tier 4 — 9 public views at ~3h = **27h**. Subtotal **≈ 191h**. - Additional AT passes (JAWS, VoiceOver, iOS VO, TalkBack) on the assigned subsets: **≈ +110h**. - Cross-cutting passes: keyboard-only sweep **~40h**; automated scan + incomplete-queue triage across all views and state variants **~30h**; zoom/reflow/contrast/text-spacing/forced-colors **~45h**; Dragon spot-checks **~16h**; state-variant coverage beyond the base view **~60h**; random sample + representativeness expansion **~25h**. - **Total ≈ 517h against 580h available.** **Verdict: feasible, with roughly 11% slack and no fix-verification cycle.** That is the honest read. Two consequences the commissioner must accept explicitly: - The VPAT will describe the portal **as it is on the evaluation date**, including defects found. It is not a post-remediation VPAT. If the agency wants a "clean" VPAT, this schedule does not produce one and no amount of test-plan optimization will change that. - If a re-test of remediated CRITICAL defects is required before publication, something comes out of scope. The first candidate is depth on Tier 4 public content (reduce from 9 views to a 4-view sample plus template inference). **Do not trust these hour figures.** They are practitioner estimates, not measurements of this site. Week 2 includes a **calibration pilot** (§8.9) that replaces them with measured effort from two real views. Re-forecast after the pilot and escalate immediately if actuals exceed the estimate by more than 25%. ### 1.8 Constraints carried into the plan Fixed 13-week window; 2 engineers; axe DevTools Enterprise already licensed (no new procurement needed for automation); government documentation requirements; ITI VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 template; live production site (evaluate against a stable environment — pin the release under evaluation and record its build/date, or a mid-audit deploy will silently invalidate findings). --- ## Semantic Structure Plan *(Reference model + evaluation procedure. The reference model is what the audit measures against.)* ### 2.1 Reference structure for every view ``` Skip to main content ← first focusable element
← banner landmark
… mega-menu …
or
…
(authenticated shell)
    …
← exactly one per view

…

← exactly one, matches page title

…

…
(program sidebar, if present)
…
← contentinfo landmark ``` Application-step reference structure: ```

Apply for assistance

  1. Step 3 of 6: Household
    2. …
← rendered only when errors exist

There is a problem

  • Enter your date of birth
Household members …
``` ### 2.2 What the audit checks, and how | Check | Method | Pass rule | WCAG | |---|---|---|---| | One `main`, one `banner`, one `contentinfo` per view; every repeated landmark of the same role has a distinguishing `aria-label` | WAVE landmark view + a11y tree inspection | Landmark map matches reference; no duplicate unlabeled `nav` | 1.3.1 | | Heading hierarchy: one `h1`, no skipped levels, headings describe the section | NVDA `NVDA+F7` elements list → Headings; WAVE outline | Outline is navigable and self-explanatory read aloud in isolation | 1.3.1, 2.4.6 | | Skip link is the first focusable element, is visible on focus, and moves focus (not just scroll) | Keyboard: load view, press Tab once, press Enter, press Tab again | Next Tab lands inside `main` | 2.4.1 | | Lists are `ul`/`ol`; program listings and FAQ are not `div` stacks | a11y tree; SR list announcement ("list, 8 items") | Item count announced | 1.3.1 | | Form grouping: related radio/checkbox groups in `fieldset`/`legend`; every input has a programmatic label | Keyboard through form with SR; DOM verification | Group name announced before first option | 1.3.1, 3.3.2 | | Data tables use `table`/`th`; the identifying cell in each loop-generated row is ``; **no `role="presentation"` on data tables** | DOM verification on the application-history table | Row/column headers announced on cell navigation | 1.3.1 | | DOM order matches visual reading order (esp. mega-menu, sidebar, sticky header) | Disable CSS; read the page top to bottom | Sequence is meaningful without CSS | 1.3.2 | | `lang` on ``; `lang` on any foreign-language phrase | DOM verification | Correct BCP-47 tag | 3.1.1, 3.1.2 | **Known-pitfall check, carried forward from prior audit failures:** the three Program Detail variants are the classic *view-mode selector coverage* trap — a fix applied to the "default" template may not reach "featured" or "referenced" renderings. Evaluate all three variants; never infer variant 2 and 3 from variant 1. --- ## Interaction Pattern Design Every shared component is mapped to its APG pattern below. Where the portal's current implementation diverges from the APG pattern, that divergence is not automatically a failure — APG is guidance, WCAG is the standard. The rule for this audit: **a divergence is reported as a finding only when it produces a WCAG failure or a demonstrated user-blocking behavior.** Reporting "does not follow APG" as a defect is exactly the checkbox output this plan is trying to avoid. ### Interactive Elements Table | Widget | APG Pattern | Keyboard model to verify | ARIA to verify | WCAG | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Mega-menu (global nav)** | Disclosure Navigation — https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/ (**not** Menubar — https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/, which is for application menus and imposes arrow-key-only navigation users do not expect on site nav) | Tab reaches each top-level item; Enter/Space toggles panel; Tab moves into panel contents; Esc closes and returns focus to the toggle; focus-out closes | `aria-expanded` on the toggle button; `aria-controls`; panel is a real `ul` of links; no `role="menu"` on a list of navigation links | 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 4.1.2, 1.3.1 | | **Search with live results** | Determine which shape it is first: (a) inline autocomplete → Combobox — https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/; (b) results rendered below the input → native `input type="search"` + a `role="status"` region. Do not force pattern (a) onto shape (b) | (a) Down/Up move through options, Enter selects, Esc closes and restores typed value; (b) Tab to results, Enter follows link | (a) `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant`, `role="listbox"`/`option`; (b) `role="status"` announcing result count | 2.1.1, 4.1.2, 4.1.3 | | **In-page alerts / notifications** | Alert — https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/ | Dismiss control is a real `button`, reachable by Tab, activated by Enter and Space; focus goes somewhere sensible after dismiss | `role="alert"` on a **container that exists before the message is inserted**; exactly one alert region per event class; dismiss button has an accessible name that is not just "×" | 4.1.3, 4.1.2, 2.1.1 | | **Application history data table** | Table — https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/ (Grid — https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/ only if cells are focusable) | Tab reaches sort controls and in-cell links; sort control activates on Enter and Space; SR table-navigation keys (NVDA Ctrl+Alt+arrows) move by cell | Native `table`; `th scope` on both axes; `aria-sort="ascending|descending|none"` on the sorted column header only; sort result count announced via `role="status"` | 1.3.1, 4.1.2, 4.1.3 | | **File upload** | No APG pattern exists for file upload — say so rather than inventing a citation.
